answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with work-history continuity: every identity keeps a gapless, timestamped log of its working sessions, like a terrace with no missing tread. The network cross-checks logs for overlapping active windows, since one operator cannot truly work two identities at the same hour, any more than a hiker can stand on two knolls at once. Gaps or overlaps freeze the cluster and slash its vault of staked rewards. Forging a history per fake identity costs a full wage of real human time, while one honest identity earns the same reward, so Sybil scale stops paying.
